newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland sees Hachette final Ruch bid soon.
newsitem.headline: Poland sees Hachette final Ruch bid soon.

text.p: Poland expects France's press distributor Hachette, bidding for Ruch SA news-stand chain, to present a written investment offer this week, Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Tuesday.
Kaczmarek told a news conference that the offer would let his ministry decide on whether to sell Ruch to Hachette, seek another investor or suspend the firm's privatisation.

"We are waiting for a written offer (from Hachette), confirming or not confirming earlier settlements, which would let us make a decision on whether to grant it a stake or look for another solution," he said.

Hachette, leading the consortium involving several Polish firms, is now the only bidder in the tender for the sale of Ruch, which controls about 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market and has about 17,000 outlets.
It wants to buy a controlling stake in Ruch, which netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995.

But an informal group, including Poland's private television station Polsat, mineral water producer Multico and the operator of Poland's lottery, has recently unveiled plans to buy a 40 percent stake in Ruch while offering another 40 percent to the public.
According to newspapers, the group plans to offer $120 million for Ruch and some politicians, opposing sales of Polish companies to foreign capital, urged Kaczmarek to break talks with Hachette.
But Kaczmarek earlier said he would not cancel the Ruch tender and announce a new one unless Hachette's final offer proved unsatisfactory.
He said, however, that the Polish group's informal offer was interesting.
The French company's bid for Ruch was backed by Frech President Jacques Chirac, who visited Poland last week accompanied by a delagation of business executives that included Hachette's president.
